topic: Fixed-initial-rank finiteness at arXiv:2501.14643v1, Section 1, page 2, and its general and particular subclasses
title: Infinitely many general rank sequences: extending Patel's polynomiality picture (2026) at arXiv:2501.14643v1, Section 1, p. 2

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending Patel's (2026) polynomiality picture, we disprove the finiteness conjecture of Rowland and Sistos Barrón at arXiv:2501.14643v1, Section 1, p. 2: every initial rank r >= 3 admits infinitely many general rank sequences, realized by positive integer sequences. Their ranks are binomial(M+r-1,r-1) - binomial(M-K+r-1,r-1), with the second term zero when M < K, so arbitrarily long maximal prefixes do not determine the full rank sequence. A different family, s_p(n) = p*8^n - 4^n - 2^n, gives infinitely many particular rank sequences under one fixed rank-three recurrence, by parameter-dependent coefficient cancellation. These conclusions concern the number of entire rank sequences, rather than their individual eventual polynomiality.
summary: Positive integer sequences realize infinitely many general rank sequences at each initial rank r >= 3, and infinitely many particular rank-three rank sequences under one common recurrence. Full proofs give exact ranks, arbitrarily long shared prefixes, and explicit homogeneous relation groups.

posing_source.title: Complexity of powers of a constant-recursive sequence
posing_source.locator: Section 1, page 2; definitions in Section 2, pages 3–4

coverage.main_statement: For each r >= 3, the positive integer sequences 1 + 2^n + 2^(K*n) + sum(q_i^n), K >= 2, with r-3 distinct odd primes q_i, have infinitely many distinct general rank sequences.
coverage.exact_rank: H_(r,K)(M) = binomial(M+r-1,r-1) - binomial(M-K+r-1,r-1), with the second term zero for M < K.
coverage.fixed_recurrence_statement: The positive integer family s_p(n) = p*8^n - 4^n - 2^n, p >= 3, has infinitely many rank sequences and satisfies s(n+3) = 14*s(n+2) - 56*s(n+1) + 64*s(n).
coverage.formal_statement: Negation of fixed-rank finiteness for integer-valued sequences with rational tail recurrences and every positive exponent; the proof specializes to the rank-three family s_p.
written_proofs: The Vandermonde lower bound for distinct nonzero rational exponential bases, including tail recurrences and complex recurrence coefficients
Fixed-recurrence coefficient-support formula, finite exceptional parameter sets, designated cancellation, and finite parameter fibres
Positive integer sequences and the common recurrence for s_p
Infinitely many particular rank sequences agreeing with 2*M+1 through any prescribed finite exponent
The same particular rank sequences for every integer base b >= 2
The all-rank general-family formula by unique canonical product representations
Infinitely many general rank sequences sharing arbitrarily long maximal binomial prefixes
Exact homogeneous relation subgroup Z*(K-1,-K,1,0,...,0), with free quotient rank r-1
